title: FastAPI docs: Deta deployment instructions may be outdated
body: ### First Check - [X] I added a very descriptive title here. - [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it. - [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search. - [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information. - [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer. - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc). ### Commit to Help - [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆 ### Example Code ```python iwr https://get.deta.dev/cli.ps1 -useb | iex curl -fsSL https://get.deta.dev/cli.sh | sh https://fastapi.xiniushu.com/ko/deployment/deta/ ``` ### Description Deta Space hosting for FastAPI no longer works because Deta has shut down its free hosting service. The current FastAPI deployment documentation still mentions Deta (for example: https://fastapi.xiniushu.com/ko/deployment/deta/) and includes CLI install commands: - iwr https://get.deta.dev/cli.ps1 -useb | iex - curl -fsSL https://get.deta.dev/cli.sh | sh These commands now fail because the domain get.deta.dev no longer resolves. Could the documentation be updated to reflect that Deta deployment is no longer possible, or replaced with an alternative hosting method? ### Operating System Windows ### Operating System Details Windows 11 Home 64-bit (Version 22H2) ### FastAPI Version 0.116.1 ### Pydantic Version 2.11.7 ### Python Version 3.12.6 ### Additional Context I was following the deployment instructions in the FastAPI documentation for Deta. However, when I tried to install the Deta CLI as per the docs, the download links are no longer working (get.deta.dev cannot be resolved), and the Deta website now only offers a desktop download, it no longer shows the Deta Space hosting option. It seems Deta has discontinued their online app hosting platform, so the documentation may need to be updated or marked as deprecated.

It seems Deta has discontinued their online app hosting platform, so the documentation may need to be updated or marked as deprecated.
